family: The exactly-one counting family, defined in proof.md Section 1: for every integer n>=0 (no exceptions, including f_0(empty)=0 since the empty string has zero ones), f_n(x)=1 iff x in {0,1}^n contains exactly one 1. Language L={x in {0,1}*: |x|_1 = 1}, decided by one fixed linear-time counter; NP verifier V(x,w)=1 iff w is empty and |x|_1=1, witness bound W(n)=0.
theorem: For this one total uniform linear-time family, hence in NP with empty witnesses, C_B2(f_n)>=2n-3 for every integer n>=2 in the full Li–Yang B2 model at actual input length n=|x|; hence liminf C_B2(f_n)/n>=2.
